title: Sentinel shims per tenant/model/region for safe fallbacks and load-shedding
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: During cross-region capacity events and degraded upstream dependencies we need deterministic, low-latency decisions to degrade gracefully. Existing global circuit logic has too coarse granularity (service-level) and causes either noisy full-service trips or slow reaction times for tenant/model hotspots. This ticket proposes a lightweight per-entity 'sentinel shim' layer that makes fast circuit decisions (trip/repair/hedge/shed) scoped to tenant+model+region and coordinates with the global circuit fabric for SLO preservation and safe multi-region failover.
proposal: Introduce ephemeral sentinel shims collocated with regional edge proxies. Each shim holds small in-memory circuits keyed by tenant_id|model_id|region. Shims evaluate short-window metrics (1m/5m) for error-rate, queue-depth, p95/p99 latency and model-specific quality regressions. On trip, the shim executes a configured fallback policy (prefer local cache -> smaller model variant -> queue-shed -> redirect to secondary region) and emits a trip token to the global control plane to inform routing decisions and long-term mitigation.
design_decisions:
- Scope: circuits are per (tenant, model, region) with optional global aggregation.
- Windows: fast window (1m) for quick trips; confirmation window (5m) before long-term global flag.
- Trip criteria (defaults): error_rate >= 4% over 1m OR p99 latency >= 2s over 1m OR queue_length > 200 requests.
- Hysteresis: require metrics to be under 50% of trip thresholds for 2 consecutive windows to auto-close.
- Cooldown/backoff: 30s initial cooldown, exponential backoff up to 20m before re-evaluating more aggressively.
- Fallback priority: cached-response hit -> smaller quantized model variant -> routed to dedicated reserved pool (if tenant has capacity) -> region failover -> synthetic 503 with explanatory header.
- Observability contract: shims must export counts for trip_events, fallback_hits, local_shed_count, failover_redirects, and per-entity SLO breach counters.
implementation_plan:
1) Library: implement sentinel shim library (Go) with pluggable metric backends and a tiny on-heap circuit store.
2) Integration: wire shim into edge proxy (ingress path) with a non-blocking fast-path check.
3) Control plane: emit trip events as compact protobuf to existing event bus (topic: shim-trips).
4) Policies: implement per-tenant policy records persisted in control plane (fallback order, thresholds overrides).
5) Tests: unit tests + integration test harness simulating noisy tenant and region outages.
6) Canary: enable for 10 tenants in us-west-2 for 48h, then widen to 100 tenants and enable region failover in controlled ratio.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 0 (dev): library + unit tests only.
- Phase 1 (staging): integration with edge proxy behind feature flag. Run synthetic failure scenarios.
- Phase 2 (canary): enable for small tenant set in us-west-2 and monitor fallback and SLO impact for 72h.
- Phase 3 (regional expansion): add us-east-1, eu-west-1 with progressive traffic (1% -> 5% -> 25%).
- Phase 4 (global): flip default on for all tenants but keep per-tenant opt-out for first 2 weeks.
- Rollback: feature flag off disables shim decisions and drains trip tokens; control-plane aggregator removes global flags after TTL.
acceptance_criteria:
- Shim library implemented and code-reviewed.
- Integration tests show correct per-entity trips for simulated error and latency patterns.
- Metrics available on dashboards: shim.trip_events, shim.fallback_hits, shim.shed_rate, shim.failover_redirects.
- During canary the overall platform p99 latency and error-rate do not regress more than 1% compared to baseline.
- Runbook validated: on a shim trip we can identify entity key, reason, and executed fallback within 30s from dashboard.
tests:
- Unit tests for circuit state transitions (closed->open->half-open->closed) including hysteresis.
- E2E harness: inject 5xx burst to model workers and assert shim trips and fallback path executed.
- Chaos: kill region worker pool to validate region failover orchestration (cache warm, request staging).
- Performance: shim check must add <200us median latency on the request path in p95 test.
monitoring_and_alerting:
Dashboards: per-region heatmap of open circuits and per-tenant top 20 circuit hitters. Required metrics: shim_open_count, shim_open_rate, shim_trip_reasons (error|latency|queue), shim_fallback_distribution.
Alerts:
- P0 alert: region-wide open-circuit ratio > 10% for > 5m.
- P1 alert: single-tenant open-circuit count > 5 in 1m (possible noisy neighbor).
- P2: fallback_rate > 2% platform-wide sustained > 30m.
- SLO alert: SLO breach rate increase > 0.5% absolute relative to baseline caused by shim action.
runbook:
When alerted about region-wide open circuits:
1) Query dashboard for top-tenant keys and trip reasons.
2) If noisy neighbor, engage tenant team and escalate to quota throttling or reserved capacity offer.
3) If backend model process crashed, trigger regional restart and initiate guided cache warm (preload common prefixes).
4) If region-wide capacity exhausted, enable region failover policy (automated by control-plane) and monitor for cache-miss surge.
5) Postmortem: capture decision timeline from shim-trips topic and include in incident timeline.
notes:
- The sentinel shim model is intentionally small and ephemeral to reduce blast radius and keep fail decisions local and fast.
- This approach reduces the number of global circuit toggles and improves latency for fallback decisions at the edge.
- We should align default thresholds with SRE-runbook SLOs and allow tenant overrides for paying customers.
